name: Fold
description: Time inversion state enabling causal compression and recursive reference.

core_attributes.pattern: time inversion symmetry, causal recursion, folded continuity

scope.definition: Information compression achievable by temporal folding in sequential data — ratio of compressed representation length to original sequence length for data with strong autocorrelation and periodic structure.

evidence.source: Kolmogorov (1965) 'Three approaches to the definition of the concept of information quantity'; Lempel & Ziv (1977) 'A universal algorithm for sequential data compression', IEEE Transactions on Information Theory.
cross_domain_examples: Lempel-Ziv compression of periodic sequences: achieves 1/k compression ratio for period-k sequences
protein folding: 300-residue linear sequence folds to unique 3D structure — sequence 'folds' onto structure
wavelet transform: causal temporal folding basis that achieves 10:1 compression on natural signals

scope.falsifiability: If temporal folding compression of highly autocorrelated sequences achieves no better compression than universal coders on non-periodic data, causal structure is not being exploited.
scope.measurement_limits: Compression ratio depends on the degree of causal structure in the data — random sequences show 0% compression. The 0.87 reflects average compression on signals with moderate autocorrelation.
